cards.text: Jesus just opened the eyes of a man born blind, and the Pharisees threw that man out (John 9:1-34). Some Pharisees are standing right there with Jesus (John 9:40). Now He paints a picture for them: a sheepfold, a gate and some sheep.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, somebody skips the gate and climbs into the sheepfold some other way. What does Jesus call him?
True or false: In Jesus' picture, the one who comes in by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.

cards.text: The gatekeeper opens the gate for the shepherd, and the sheep listen for his voice. They're like me waiting on the oven timer, friend. EARS UP.

cards.question: The shepherd calls his own sheep by ___ and leads them out.

cards.text: So the shepherd leads them out. Once all his own sheep are out of the fold, the whole flock is on the move.

cards.question: The shepherd has brought out all his sheep. Where does he walk?

cards.text: And the sheep follow him, because they know his voice. It's like a friend yelling your name across a packed parking lot: you don't even look up, your feet just GO.
Now a stranger shows up, and the sheep don't recognize his voice. Same sheep, same fold, brand-new voice they've NEVER heard.

cards.question: A stranger's voice reaches the sheep. What does Jesus say they'll do?
True or false: When Jesus finishes His sheep illustration, the people listening understand what He's telling them.

cards.text: They don't get it, so Jesus speaks to them again, and this time He puts Himself right in the picture. Me? When I get blank stares, I just say the same thing LOUDER.

cards.question: When Jesus explains again, which part of the picture does He say He is?

cards.text: Then Jesus says all who came before Him were thieves and robbers. Remember that guy climbing in some other way? Turns out he's got COMPANY.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the sheep listened to the thieves and robbers who came before Him.
Jesus says He is the gate. Anyone who enters through Him will be ___.

cards.text: That one will come in and go out and find pasture. The thief, though? He comes only to steal and kill and destroy.

cards.question: The thief comes to steal and kill and destroy. Jesus says He came so the sheep could have ___ in all its fullness.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'I am the good shepherd.' The gate AND the shepherd, friend, He's two parts of this picture now!

cards.question: Jesus says He is the good shepherd. What does the good shepherd do for the sheep?

answers.text: Lays down His life for them

cards.text: Next Jesus brings in the hired hand. He's not the shepherd, and the sheep aren't his own.

cards.question: When the hired hand sees the wolf coming, he ___ the sheep.

cards.text: He runs away, and the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock. The hired hand is GONE: no clocking out, no jacket, no goodbye, just GONE.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the hired hand runs away because he doesn't care about the sheep.

cards.text: Then Jesus says that line again: 'I am the good shepherd.' He knows His sheep and His sheep know Him, like that barber who sees you walk in and just NODS, because you've been getting the same cut for twelve years.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus compares knowing His sheep to the way He and the Father know each other.

cards.text: He says once more that He lays down His life for the sheep. Then He says He has other sheep that are not of this fold, and He must bring them in as well.

cards.question: Jesus says His other sheep, the ones not of this fold, will listen to His ___.
Once Jesus brings in His other sheep, how many flocks will there be?

cards.text: Then Jesus tells why the Father loves Him. It has to do with Him laying down His life.

cards.question: Jesus lays down His life for a purpose. What does He say it is?

answers.text: To rest from all His work

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says someone will take His life from Him.

cards.text: No one takes it. He lays it down of His own accord, with authority to lay it down and to take it up again, a charge He received from His Father.

Jesus' message causes division among the Jews again, the kind where a group chat splits right down the middle and NOBODY leaves the chat. Many of them say, 'He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?'

cards.question: Many say Jesus is demon-possessed and insane, but others disagree. What do they point to?

answers.text: A demon can't open blind eyes
The Pharisees all agree with Him

cards.text: They say, 'Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?' Friend, there's a man out there who was blind and now he sees, and he'll tell you so himself (John 9:25).

findings.problem: Story cards 4, 12, 14 and 17 each contain three standalone sentence units, including short interjections such as 'EARS UP.' and 'Me?'. None is the opening card, so each exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The preceding cards establish that the sheep listen for the shepherd's voice, but they give no basis for choosing 'name' over 'number' or 'whistle'. The blank asks for unseen wording from John 10:3 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but 'Right behind them' and 'Beside the gatekeeper' are invented positions rather than real details drawn from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: John 10:5 says the sheep do not recognize the stranger's voice. The card turns that into a voice they have 'NEVER heard', adding a certainty the text does not give; this is storyteller narration, not a clearly marked joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: No earlier card explains what entering through Jesus accomplishes, so the baker has no contextual basis for choosing 'saved' over 'tested' or 'judged'. This completes the unseen wording of John 10:9 instead of testing a meaning established by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
